rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the impurity as divine displeasure.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: أي سخط من عمل الشيطان

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr explains rijس as sin.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: إثم

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam glosses the impurity as evil from Satan’s work.
rows.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: أي شر من عمل الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers back to the impurity; the command means to leave it.
rows.anchor: الضمير عائد على الرجس، أي اتركوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of success is encouragement to comply with the command.
rows.anchor: أي اتركوه {لعلكم تفلحون} وهذا ترغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning about Satan’s aims in wine and gambling is a threat and deterrent.
rows.anchor: فهل أنتم منتهون} وهذا تهديد وترهيب

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra recounts the staged ban: first 2:219, then 4:43 after an intoxicated prayer leader recited confusedly, and finally this verse, after which people stopped.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: حرمت الخمر ثلاث مرات، قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: When asked about believers who died before the final prohibition while drinking and gambling, 5:93 was revealed; the Prophet said they would have left it had it been forbidden to them.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى: {ليس على الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جناح فيما طعموا}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that at the conquest a Thaqafī or Dawsī friend brought the Prophet wine; the Prophet said its prohibition also forbids its sale, and it was poured out.
rows.anchor: سألت ابن عباس عن بيع الخمر

rows.speaker: تميم الداري
rows.claim: Tamīm al-Dārī’s annual wine gift was rejected after the ban; the Prophet cursed Jews for melting forbidden fat to sell it and said wine and its price are forbidden. A second route is given through ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ghanm.
rows.anchor: عن تميم الداري أنه كان يهدي لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم راوية

rows.speaker: قيس بن سعد بن عبادة
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to have forbidden wine, kubah, and qinīn, and warned against ghubayrāʾ, which he called a third of the world’s wine.
rows.anchor: عن قيس بن سعد بن عبادة؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن ربي تبارك وتعالى حرم علي الخمر

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet lists wine, gambling, mizr, kubah, and qinīn as forbidden, and adds that witr prayer was specially given to him; Yazīd explains qinīn as lutes. Aḥmad alone reports it.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله حرم على أمتي الخمر

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: The Prophet warns against attributing words to him falsely, says wine, gambling, kubah, and ghubayrāʾ are forbidden, and declares every intoxicant unlawful; Aḥmad alone reports it.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من قال علي ما لم أقل

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that wine is cursed in ten roles: its drinker, server, seller, buyer, presser, commissioner, carrier, recipient, and one who consumes its price, as well as wine itself.
rows.anchor: ابن عمر يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لعنت الخمر على عشرة وجوه

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar recounts the Prophet cutting open wine containers at the market and cursing wine and those involved in its production, sale, transport, service, and price.
rows.anchor: سمعت ابن عمر يقول: خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى المربد

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: The Prophet had Ibn ʿUmar sharpen a blade, then ordered him and companions to cut every wine container in Medina’s markets, including imported wine.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمر: أمرني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن آتيه بمدية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās rules that wine and its price are forbidden.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس، فسألته عن الخمر وثمنها، فقال: هي حرام وثمنها حرام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that if another scripture and prophet were to follow this Qurʾān and Prophet, this community would have received the same severe prohibition as earlier peoples; its matter is deferred to Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: ثم قال ابن عباس، رضي الله عنه: يا معشر أمة محمد، إنه لو كان كتاب بعد كتابكم

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar recounts the Prophet gathering and identifying wine, cursing all ten parties connected to it, then puncturing the skins despite their usefulness because he acted in anger at God’s displeasure; he refused ʿUmar’s offer to do it.
rows.anchor: قال ثابت: فلقيت عبد الله بن عمر فسألته عن ثمن الخمر، فقال: سأخبرك عن الخمر

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: A wine carrier from Khaybar asks whether he may return his stock or give it away after the ban; the Prophet refuses both, and the man pours it out. Ibn Kathīr calls this report gharīb.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: كان رجل يحمل الخمر

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: When the carrier says orphans in his care own some of the wine, the Prophet promises replacement from Bahrain’s funds when they arrive.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: كان رجل يحمل الخمر

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: The Prophet allows people to use the wine vessels by untying their openings; the wine is emptied into a valley.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: كان رجل يحمل الخمر

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Abū Ṭalḥa asks about orphans who inherited wine; the Prophet orders it poured out and refuses the suggestion to turn it into vinegar. The report is also transmitted by Muslim, Abū Dāwūd, and al-Tirmidhī.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك؛ أن أبا طلحة سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أيتام في حجره ورثوا خمرا فقال: "أهرقها"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr grades the preceding report from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr about the verse’s Torah parallel as having a sound chain.
rows.anchor: وهذا إسناد صحيح. حديث آخر: قال عبد الله بن وهب

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: A report says that missing prayer while drunk once is like losing the world; doing so four times merits the clay of ruin, explained as the extract of Hell’s inhabitants.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من ترك الصلاة سكرا مرة واحدة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to say every fermented drink is wine and every intoxicant forbidden; intoxication reduces prayer for forty mornings, and after a fourth offense merits Hell’s pus. He also threatens whoever gives intoxicants to a young child.
rows.anchor: عن طاوس، عن ابن عباس، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "كل مخمر خمر، وكل مسكر حرام، ومن شرب مسكرا بخست

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that a person who drinks wine and does not repent will be deprived of it in the afterlife; another report says an unrepentant addict who dies will not drink it there.
rows.anchor: عن نافع، عن ابن عمر، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من شرب الخمر في الدنيا، ثم لم يتب منها حرمها في الآخرة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: The Prophet says God will not look on Judgment Day at one disobedient to parents, an addicted wine drinker, or a person who boasts of gifts.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن يسار؛ أنه سمع سالم بن عبد الله يقول: قال عبد الله بن عمر: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ثلاثة لا ينظر الله إليهم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: A report from Abū Saʿīd says that a boastful giver, a person disobedient to parents, and a wine addict will not enter Paradise; Aḥmad and al-Nasāʾī transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "لا يدخل الجنة منان ولا عاق، ولا مدمن خمر

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Another report says Paradise is barred to one disobedient to parents, a wine addict, a boastful giver, and a child of zina.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "لا يدخل الجنة عاق، ولا مدمن خمر، ولا منان، ولا ولد زنية

rows.speaker: البخاري
rows.claim: Al-Bukhārī notes uncertain links in the report’s chain: no known hearing between Jabān and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, Salim and Jabān, or Nabit and Jabān; Ibn Kathīr notes versions through Mujāhid from Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Hurayra.
rows.anchor: وقال البخاري: لا يعرف لجابان سماع من عبد الله، ولا لسالم من جابان

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
rows.claim: ʿUthmān warns that wine is the mother of abominations, recounting how an ascetic, lured into a woman’s home, drank wine and then committed adultery and murder; wine and faith cannot long coexist.
rows.anchor: وقال الزهري: حدثني أبو بكر بن عبد الرحمن بن الحارث بن هشام، أن أباه قال: سمعت عثمان بن عفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers are Quraysh, and what they reject is the Qurʾān brought by the Prophet with its guidance and clarification; it is the truth beyond which there is no truth.
rows.anchor: أي: بالقرآن الذي جئتهم به، والهدى والبيان. {قومك} يعني: قريشا {وهو الحق}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is neither guardian nor overseer over them: his duty is to convey, while they must listen and obey; followers prosper in both lives and opponents are wretched. The wording is linked to 18:29.
rows.anchor: أي: لست عليكم بحفيظ، ولست بموكل بكم، كقوله {وقل الحق من ربكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغير واحد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others say every report has a reality and comes to pass, even if only after time; Ibn Kathīr links this to 38:88 and 13:37.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغير واحد: أي لكل نبأ حقيقة، أي: لكل خبر وقوع، ولو بعد حين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming warning is a threat and emphatic menace.
rows.anchor: وهذا تهديد ووعيد أكيد؛ ولهذا قال بعده: {وسوف تعلمون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who engage in God’s signs are denying and mocking them; one should withdraw until they turn to another topic.
rows.anchor: أي: بالتكذيب والاستهزاء {فأعرض عنهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address applies to every member of the community: do not sit with deniers who distort God’s signs; if forgetfulness leads you to sit with them, leave once reminded.
rows.anchor: والمراد بهذا كل فرد، فرد من آحاد الأمة، ألا يجلس مع المكذبين الذين يحرفون آيات الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that error, forgetfulness, and coercion have been lifted from his community.
rows.anchor: رفع عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان وما استكرهوا عليه

rows.speaker: السدي عن أبي مالك وسعيد بن جبير ومقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Al-Suddī, reporting Abū Mālik and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and also Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān explain: if one forgets but then remembers, one must not remain with them.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي، عن أبي مالك وسعيد بن جبير في قوله: {وإما ينسينك الشيطان} قال: إن نسيت فذكرت، فلا تجلس معهم. وكذا قال مقاتل بن حيان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr identifies this verse with the instruction in 4:140 not to sit among those who deny or mock God’s revelations, since approving their talk makes one like them.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية هي المشار إليها في قوله: {وقد نزل عليكم في الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God splits grain and pits in the soil so crops grow from varied seeds and fruits of many forms, colors, and tastes from pits.
rows.anchor: أي: يشقه في الثرى فتنبت الزروع على اختلاف أصنافها من الحبوب، والثمار على اختلاف أشكالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The living plant emerges from the apparently dead, inanimate grain and pit; this is illustrated by 36:33–36.
rows.anchor: أي: يخرج النبات الحي من الحب والنوى، الذي هو كالجماد الميت، كما قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “bringing the dead from the living” is coordinated with “splitter of grain and pit”; Ibn Kathīr says the clause is first explained and then the second coordinated phrase follows.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {ومخرج الميت من الحي} معطوف على {فالق الحب والنوى} ثم فسره ثم عطف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the reported illustrations are a chicken from an egg and an egg from a chicken, or a righteous child from an unbeliever and an unbeliever from a righteous person; the verse encompasses them all.
rows.anchor: بعبارات كلها متقاربة مؤدية للمعنى، فمن قائل: يخرج الدجاجة من البيضة، والبيضة من الدجاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone, without partner, performs these acts; the verse challenges how people can turn from truth to falsehood and worship others alongside Him.
rows.anchor: ثم قال: {ذلكم الله} أي: فاعل هذه الأشياء هو الله وحده لا شريك له {فأنى تؤفكون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates light and darkness, splitting night’s darkness at dawn so the world and horizon brighten and night gives way to day; these contrasting creations display His power. The passage links to 6:1 and 7:54.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {فالق الإصباح وجاعل الليل سكنا} أي: خالق الضياء والظلام، كما قال في أول السورة: {وجعل الظلمات والنور}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is calm and dark, a time when things rest; Ibn Kathīr compares the wording with 93:1–2, 92:1–2, and 91:3–4.
rows.anchor: أي: ساجيا مظلما تسكن فيه الأشياء، كما قال: {والضحى والليل إذا سجى}

rows.speaker: صهيب الرومي
rows.claim: When his wife reproached him for staying awake, Ṣuhayb al-Rūmī said that night is rest for everyone but him: thoughts of Paradise intensify his longing, and thoughts of Hell drive away sleep.
rows.anchor: وقال صهيب الرومي [رضي الله عنه] (6) لامرأته وقد عاتبته في كثرة سهره: إن الله جعل الليل سكنا
